newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-SURGERY AIMED TO HELP KANU PLAY AGAIN, SAY DOCTORS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SURGERY AIMED TO HELP KANU PLAY AGAIN, SAY DOCTORS.

text.p: Doctors who operated on Nigerian striker Nwankwo Kanu said on Friday they had repaired his heart valve rather than replaced it in order to increase his chances of returning to soccer.

Doctors at the Cleveland Clinic Foundation in the United States said in a statement released by Kanu's Italian club, Internazionale, that the Olympic star was doing well after undergoing surgery last Monday.

"He is up and walking, and will soon begin a graduated rehabilitation programme over the next several months to bring him back to peak level," Doctor John R. Kramer was quoted as saying in the statement.

Kanu, 20, captained Nigeria's under-23 team to the gold medal at the Atlanta Olympics last summer but was sidelined shortly afterwards when doctors discovered a heart condition that threatened to kill him if he continued playing.
The statement said Kanu was born with a deformed aortic heart valve that began to leak and affect his heart function.
"The valve was repaired rather than replaced in hopes of his return to the sport," Kramer said.
"Tests performed today showed no signs of continued leaking from the valve," Kramer added.

The statement said Kanu was expected to be discharged from hospital "in the next couple of days", adding the player had expressed his gratitude for the support of fans, Inter and the people and government of Nigeria.
Inter doctor Piero Volpi earlier told reporters that doctors would have to wait four months to see if Kanu's heart, which is enlarged, returned to normal size to know if he could return to the pitch.
But the player's manager, Franklin Sedoc, said the first priority was Kanu's health and rehabilitation.

"We are taking it step by step. That's how we handled it when Kanu first learned about his heart condition, and that's how we will approach his rehabilitation," Sedoc was quoted as saying in the statement.
Kanu was quoted this week as saying "I will be back" and reported to have given the 'V' for victory sign as he was wheeled into the theatre for surgery.

Kanu, who won the European Cup with Ajax in 1995 before moving to Inter last summer, is sentimental favourite to be named African Footballer of the Year when the announcement is made in Cairo this weekend.
